attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The actual plaquette-sheet endpoint incidence table B_12,v,B_13,v,B_23,v and the uniform epsilon_v plus E_tail bounds have not yet been certified for the geometric three-hairpin collars.
steps: Start with the Schur-Feshbach-reduced null scalar S_null=M_G+z^*Rz+tails for the fixed three-hairpin block, where z=(1,1,-2).
Write z^*Rz as the weighted connected endpoint contribution with weights w_12=2, w_13=-4, w_23=-4 after diagonal normalization removes one-body Wilson factors.

Use heat-kernel plaquette-sheet localization: straight shared-boundary contractions decompose into Wick-square Gram terms plus a local C_A f f contact. The Gram part is nonnegative, and the straight f f part cancels by the null incidence identity.
The remaining local endpoint box v is described by F_v(s;b)=log Z_v(s;b). Its fourth source derivative is the singlet connected Wilson four-flux cumulant kappa_4_v(b).

Insert the compact-group small-box expansion kappa_4_v(b)=-chi_v B_v(b)+epsilon_v. Since chi_v>=0, the only negative contribution to S_null comes from endpoint boxes with D_v=2B_12,v-4B_13,v-4B_23,v positive.
This yields the valid bound S_null>=M_G-C_col sum_v chi_v[D_v]_+-remainder-tail. Equal disjoint endpoint boxes or boxes dominated by 13/23 incidence are safe rather than dangerous.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The sign mechanism is valid, but without the real endpoint table a hidden 12-dominant corner cluster or a negative nonlocal tail could still make the certified interval negative.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Endpoint kappa_4 incidence bound for the post-H,K Wilson hairpin block

assumptions: The first-order PHP gate has the one-dimensional null vector z=(1,1,-2) for the fixed three-hairpin block.
Heat-kernel endpoint localization separates straight shared-boundary contacts from endpoint/corner boxes with a uniform tail estimate E_tail.
Disconnected Wick-square contractions are kept as positive Gram terms and are not counted as dangerous connected R.
The straight nonabelian C_A f f contact has the same oriented incidence on the three entries, so the z-null incidence cancels it away from endpoints.
For each endpoint box v, the singlet projected fourth cumulant has kappa_4_v(b)=-chi_v B_v(b)+epsilon_v with chi_v>=0 and certified epsilon_v.
definitions: source object: heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulated SU(N) Wilson endpoint boxes for the already fixed three-hairpin H,K block, with reflection collar width delta and lattice scale a.
target object: the scalar post-H,K Schur-Feshbach null-channel endpoint contribution R_null that decides whether the positive Gaussian margin survives.
controlled interface: extract R_null from diagonal-normalized reflected Wilson OS entries using connected log Z_v fourth source derivatives after Wick-square and straight f f cancellations.

same-theory condition: the same heat-kernel Wilson sheet regulator, color representation, endpoint boxes, and diagonal normalization are used for H,K,R and no boundary counterterm or algebra enlargement is introduced.

equations.label: null-channel weights
equations.valid_when: Valid when the Schur-Feshbach null vector is the kernel direction of PHP for the fixed three-hairpin Wilson block.

equations.label: endpoint cumulant source
equations.valid_when: Applies after heat-kernel plaquette-sheet localization isolates one endpoint box and the source b is gauge-singlet projected.

equations.label: endpoint R scalar
equations.valid_when: Requires diagonal normalization, connected logarithms, Wick-square cancellation, and null-incidence cancellation of straight nonabelian f f contacts.

equations.label: dominance variable
equations.valid_when: Valid in the small endpoint-box heat-kernel regime where the root-Jacobian quartic term dominates the sixth-order remainder.

equations.label: safe endpoint bound
equations.valid_when: Applies when the positive Gaussian Schur margin M_G has already been computed from H and K.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A certified table with C_col sum_v chi_v[D_v]_+ > M_G plus all certified errors is a same-theory OS falsifier for this block.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Reduces the post-H,K Yang-Mills input to a finite endpoint incidence table B_ij,v, a signed compact-group kappa_4 coefficient chi_v, and a tail estimate. It explains why negative local kappa_4 alone is not a falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For the fixed three-hairpin block after H,K are known, the endpoint part of the connected boundary-OPE polarization is dangerous only through a signed endpoint-incidence dominance functional. If the compact-group fourth cumulant has the heat-kernel form kappa_4_v(b)=-chi_v B_v(b)+epsilon_v with chi_v>=0, then endpoint boxes with 2B_12,v<=4B_13,v+4B_23,v cannot demote the corrected Schur-Feshbach scalar. A valid falsifier must certify net 12-endpoint dominance large enough to exceed the positive Gaussian margin and all remainder/tail bounds.

assumptions: F_v is C^8 on the source interval |s|<=3h for the finite heat-kernel box.
The source insertion is gauge-invariant after singlet projection and uses the locked Wilson representation.
The finite-difference interval remains inside the small-field chart or is evaluated directly on the compact group.
definitions: F_v(s;b)=log Z_v(s;b) for one endpoint box and one singlet projected Wilson source direction b.
The source b_{ij,v} includes the color factor T_F, oriented plaquette-sheet incidence, and endpoint geometric corner projection.
The same endpoint finite box and heat-kernel time t_a must be used for all seven source evaluations.

equations.label: seven-point fourth derivative
equations.valid_when: Valid when the endpoint partition function is evaluated with the identical regulator and source direction at all seven points.

equations.label: stencil remainder
equations.valid_when: Applies when F_v has a bounded eighth derivative on the whole symmetric source interval.

equations.label: interval sign test
equations.valid_when: Requires that all endpoint boxes are enumerated and that the tail bound covers nonlocal corner interactions.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the certified interval I_null lies strictly below zero, the corrected second-order OS form is negative in the realized Wilson block.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Provides the concrete regulator-level computation that can promote the branch or produce a certified finite-block falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.statement: The endpoint cumulant entering the dominance bound can be certified without symbolic modeling by seven same-theory source evaluations of the endpoint-box heat-kernel partition function. The stencil kills the Gaussian part and estimates the connected fourth derivative with an eighth-derivative error bound.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot or quarantine if the endpoint geometry cannot be locked to the same Wilson regulator used for H,K, because then the R computation is not same-theory.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if the certified interval for S_null is nonnegative after inserting the real B_v table, kappa_4 stencil intervals, and tail bound.
control_decision.reason: The branch is not looping: the remaining contribution is a finite heat-kernel endpoint calculation with explicit color factor, geometry factor, stencil, and sign inequality.

dependency_updates.description: Enumerate each endpoint box v and compute B_12,v,B_13,v,B_23,v from the singlet-projected oriented plaquette-sheet sources.
Use the seven-point same-theory stencil for d_s^4 log Z_v with 7h^4 M_8/240 error to certify chi_v and epsilon_v.
Verify that the C_A f f contact has identical straight-segment incidence in the three weighted entries and only endpoint/corner residues remain.
Bound endpoint-to-endpoint and corner tails not captured by the finite boxes, with sign-sensitive control against M_G.
The closed-cone reflection-positivity passage is no longer the active bottleneck for this branch.

falsifiers: A regulator-level endpoint table with positive dominance C_col sum_v chi_v[D_v]_+ exceeding M_G plus all remainder and tail bounds is a concrete falsifier.
A same-theory seven-point computation of kappa_4_v that gives a larger negative value than the root-quartic bound permits would demote the expansion.
A failure of the straight C_A f f null-incidence cancellation at oriented corners would reintroduce a bulk connected R term not covered by the endpoint estimate.
A boundary counterterm or changed Wilson normalization between H,K and R would invalidate the same-theory condition even if the finite matrix stayed positive.
A tail estimate with negative sign and size comparable to M_G would prevent promotion despite safe local endpoint boxes.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 254 shows that the negative compact-group endpoint kappa_4 is not automatically dangerous. In the actual null channel its pair weights are 2,-4,-4, so only certified 12-endpoint dominance can overcome the positive Schur-Feshbach margin. This is a sharper valid R/kappa_4 endpoint-box test and a concrete falsifier criterion, not another restatement of the Wilson/OS obstruction ladder.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Draw the regulated three-hairpin plaquette sheets, list all endpoint boxes, compute the singlet incidence norms B_12,v,B_13,v,B_23,v, then evaluate D_+=sum_v[2B_12,v-4B_13,v-4B_23,v]_+ and the seven-point kappa_4 intervals for the boxes with D_v>0.
